findings.title: KeyError on integration.metadata["sender"] for integrations that lack sender metadata
findings.body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, the new check `pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") != integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes every existing Integration row has `sender` in its metadata. That is not true: `build_integration` only stores `sender` when `state.get("sender")` is set, and integrations created through the normal in-Sentry pipeline never have it (the PR's own test_basic_flow asserts the final metadata contains only access_token/expires_at/icon/domain_name/account_type). Only integrations created by the installation webhook carry `sender`. This code path is reachable whenever an ACTIVE Integration exists with no OrganizationIntegration — e.g. the owning organization was deleted, orphaning the Integration row — and someone then installs the same GitHub App installation into another Sentry organization. In that case `integration.metadata["sender"]` raises KeyError and the user gets a 500 instead of the intended github-integration-failed.html page, with no way to complete the install. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and define explicit fail-open/fail-closed behavior for integrations without sender metadata.

findings.title: Network/API failures during token exchange and /user fetch are unhandled and produce 500s
findings.body: OAuthLoginView.dispatch performs two outbound HTTP calls that can raise: `req = safe_urlopen(url=ghip.get_oauth_access_token_url(), data=data)` (line 423) is outside the try/except (the try only covers safe_urlread/parsing), and `authenticated_user_info = get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` (line 434) has no exception handling at all. A DNS/connection failure or timeout to github.com, or a non-JSON error body from the api.github.com/user call (resp.json() raises), will propagate out of the pipeline and return a 500 to the user, instead of the graceful github-integration-failed.html error page this PR introduces for every other verification failure. These calls should be wrapped and converted into the same error response (ideally with logging), since transient GitHub/network errors in a user-facing auth pipeline are expected.

findings.title: Fresh-install path performs no verification that the OAuth user controls the installation
findings.body: When `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises DoesNotExist, GitHubInstallation.dispatch goes straight to `pipeline.next_step()` and `build_integration` fetches `/app/installations/{installation_id}` using the GitHub App JWT — which can read ANY installation of the Sentry GitHub App. GitHub App installation IDs are sequential/enumerable, and the OAuth step only proves the attacker's own GitHub identity; on this path it is never compared to anything about the installation. So if the Integration row does not exist yet — the installation.created webhook is delayed, permanently failed to deliver, or webhooks aren't configured/reachable (self-hosted) — anyone who knows or guesses a victim's installation_id can attach the victim's GitHub organization installation to their own Sentry organization, exposing its repositories, commits, CODEOWNERS and source-linking data. The sender check added here only helps once the webhook-created row exists. Consider additionally verifying on the fresh path that the authenticated GitHub user belongs to / admins the installation's account (e.g. via the installation account and an org-membership check), rather than skipping verification entirely.

findings.title: GitHub integration install now hard-requires the github-login OAuth app to be configured
findings.body: OAuthLoginView pulls `client_id`/`client_secret` from GitHubIdentityProvider (the github-login identity OAuth app, e.g. the `github-login.client-id`/`github-login.client-secret` options), which is a separate configuration from the GitHub App (github-app.* options) that the integration previously needed. On deployments that have the GitHub App configured but never set up the github-login identity provider (a plausible self-hosted configuration), these values are None/empty: the pipeline will redirect to GitHub's authorize URL with an invalid client_id (GitHub shows an error) or the token exchange will fail, making the GitHub integration uninstallable where it previously worked. There is no feature flag, fallback, or documentation noting this new requirement. Consider gating the new step on the OAuth app being configured, or explicitly failing with a clear operator-facing error/docs update.

findings.title: No positive-path test for the sender-match flow, and no test for integrations missing sender metadata
findings.body: The new tests only cover the negative case (test_github_user_mismatch: webhook-created Integration whose sender does not match the OAuth user). There is no test that exercises the main protected flow end-to-end: installation webhook creates the Integration with a sender, the same GitHub user completes the OAuth step, the sender check passes, and the installation links successfully (the direct-from-GitHub install path). A regression that breaks legitimate installs from GitHub would not be caught. There is also no test with a pre-existing ACTIVE Integration whose metadata lacks `sender`, which would have exposed the KeyError in `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` reported separately.
